newsitem.title: USA: Vegas oddsmaker advises mix of bets on Oscar night. [CORRECTED 23:30 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Vegas oddsmaker advises mix of bets on Oscar night. [CORRECTED 23:30 GMT]

text.p: The odds are most people will not know many of the nominees at next Monday's Oscar awards so Vegas oddsmaker Lenny Del Genio is providing the following advice for wagering on the annual event:
Hedge your bets with a mix of big-name celebrities and the small, independent movies that captivated U.S. audiences in 1996.

"Just about every category is swamped with stars who most of the American public have never heard of," Del Genio said. "Almost anything can happen, but probably some blend of independent and studio movies will actually win."

Del Genio, who has figured odds on Academy Award nominees for 16 years at Bally's Las Vegas casino, said independent films, which lack the backing of one of seven major Hollywood studios such as Warner Bros., Walt Disney Co. or Universal, have been gaining steadily over the last five years. But he is reluctant to give them an edge over some well-established stars and studios.

For best movie, Del Genio put even money odds on both "The English Patient" and "Shine". While "The English Patient" has the pedigree of an independent film because it was produced by one-time king of independents Miramax, it also has the major studio muscle that is sometimes needed to sway Academy voters because Miramax is owned by Disney.
"Shine" fits the true definition of an independent movie. It was produced on a shoestring budget through years of toiling and ingenuity by its makers.
Both movies, Del Genio says, are equally extraordinary.
"Jerry Maguire," the Tom Cruise film about a sports agent, is given 3-to-1 odds, "Fargo" 5-to-1 and "Secrets & Lies" 8-to-1.

In the best actor category, Del Genio is laying even money on Geoffrey Rush in "Shine" and Billy Bob Thornton in "Sling Blade". Both films are truly of independent origin, but more importantly both men play characters with mental disabilities the Oscar has always favoured actors in such roles.
(Corrects description of characters from "physically challenged").

He gives Tom Cruise 3-to-1 odds although many people in Hollywood think Cruise's large body of work may push him over the top. In past years Academy voters have given Oscars to actors who have been nominated many times but have never won.
"I don't believe that's the case for Tom Cruise," Del Genio said. "Now, it may be the case for Lauren Bacall in the best supporting actress category."

Bacall, who started in movies at the age of 19 and was married to Humphrey Bogart, is nearly a living legend of the silver screen, but she has yet to win an Oscar. She is nominated this year in "The Mirror Has Two Faces" and Del Genio puts her chances at even money.
While Vegas oddsmakers are well-known for trying to predict a winner, Nevada Law prohibits actual betting on all events other than sporting events.
Del Genio's favourites in top categories include:

Geoffrey Rush, "Shine" Even Money
Billy Bob Thornton, "Sling Blade" Even Money
Tom Cruise, "Jerry Maguire" 3-to-1

Woody Harrelson, "The People vs. Larry Flynt" 8-to-1 Best performance by an actress in a leading role:

Kristin Scott Thomas, "The English Patient" Even Money
